```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Petkova_2022_doxycycline_chicken"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Petkova_2022_doxycycline_chicken"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics14112440> (open access)
* Supplement (Tables S1-S4): <https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/pharmaceutics14112440/s1>

Petkova et al. gave doxycycline hyclate to 40-day-old Ross broilers through the
drinking water at the registered dose rate of 20 mg/kg/24 h for five days. Half
of the birds had been challenged with *Mycoplasma gallisepticum* at one day of
age, and half of each health group also received N-acetylcysteine (NAC,
100 mg/kg/24 h) in the feed. The authors fitted a two-compartment model with
first-order absorption, an absorption lag and first-order elimination in
Phoenix 8.3.4 (FOCE-ELS), parameterised in micro-constants (`ka`, `V/F`, `ke`,
`k12`, `k21`, `tlag`). Neither infection nor NAC was retained as a covariate,
so the final model has none. All parameters are apparent (oral) and per kg
body weight.

**Read the Errata section before using this model for dose prediction.** The
printed `V/F` and `ke` imply an apparent clearance of 0.728 L/kg/h, which
reproduces only about half of the paper's own observed exposure under the
stated once-daily regimen. The model is packaged exactly as printed; the
vignette quantifies the gap.

# Population

Thirty-two broilers contributed to the population analysis (Section 2.2): six
healthy birds on doxycycline alone (2.79 +/- 0.17 kg), six healthy birds on
doxycycline + NAC (2.84 +/- 0.29 kg), ten infected birds on doxycycline alone
(2.47 +/- 0.27 kg) and ten infected birds on doxycycline + NAC
(2.48 +/- 0.43 kg). The medicated water was freshly prepared every 12 h and the
consumed volume was recorded; the doses actually received were 24.41, 23.70,
22.18 and 23.78 mg/kg/24 h. Blood was sampled at 0.5-24 h on the first day and
at 120-174 h after the start of treatment (19 samples per healthy bird, 9-10
per infected bird). Plasma doxycycline was measured by LC-MS/MS (LOQ
0.08 ug/mL); the 4.6% of samples below the LOQ were excluded from the fit. Both
sexes were used; the sex mix was not reported.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Petkova_2022_doxycycline_chicken")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (ka) | log(0.093) 1/h | Table 1, `tvka` |
| `lvc` (V/F per kg) | log(4.73) L/kg | Table 1, `tvV/F` |
| `lkel` (ke) | log(0.154) 1/h | Table 1, `tvke` |
| `lk12` (k12) | log(4.59) 1/h | Table 1, `tvk12` |
| `lk21` (k21) | log(7.06) 1/h | Table 1, `tvk21` |
| `ltlag` (tlag) | log(0.80) h | Table 1, `tvtlag` |
| `etalka` | 0.002 | Table 2, variance of eta ka |
| `etalvc` | 0.06 | Table 2, variance of eta V |
| `etalkel` | 1.02e-7 | Table 2, variance of eta ke |
| `etalk12` | 0.32 | Table 2, variance of eta k12 |
| `etalk21` | 0.14 | Table 2, variance of eta k21 |
| `etaltlag` | 0.79 | Table 2, variance of eta tlag |
| `propSd` | 0.388 | Table 1, `tvCMultStdev` (multiplicative residual SD) |
| `addSd` | 0.121 ug/mL | Table 1, `stdev0` (additive residual SD) |
| `P_i = tvP x exp(eta_i)` for every parameter | n/a | Equation 2 and the sentence after it ("The other parameters were calculated with the same algorithm") |
| Two compartments, first-order absorption with lag, first-order elimination, micro-constant parameterisation | n/a | Section 2.6 |
| Combined additive + multiplicative residual error (`combined2`) | n/a | Section 2.6 ("a multiplicative and additive error"); Table 1 footnote |
| No covariates | n/a | Section 2.6 and Results ("The tested co-variables did not improve the model and were excluded") |
| Dose in mg/kg into `depot` | n/a | Section 2.2 |

# Observed data (Supplementary Tables S2 and S3)

The individual concentrations of all 32 birds are transcribed below. A value
printed with "(<LOQ)" is written here as `<value` and treated as missing, as in
the fit; a dash (bird not sampled at that time) is written as `.`.

```{r observed}
read_block <- function(txt, ids) {
  df <- utils::read.table(
    text = txt,
    header = FALSE,
    na.strings = ".",
    colClasses = "character"
  )
  names(df) <- c("time", paste0("chicken_", ids))
  df |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "id", values_to = "raw") |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(raw)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      time = as.numeric(time),
      id = as.integer(sub("chicken_", "", id)),
      blq = startsWith(raw, "<"),
      conc = ifelse(blq, NA_real_, suppressWarnings(as.numeric(raw)))
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, conc, blq)
}
```

# How the dose was recorded

Doxycycline was taken up with the drinking water, and the water was freshly
prepared every 12 h. The paper states the regimen as 20 mg/kg/24 h and gives
the actually received daily doses, but does not say how the intake was entered
as dose records in the Phoenix data set. The simulations below therefore carry
two readings side by side:

* **Stated regimen (q24).** The group's received daily dose as an oral bolus
  every 24 h, five doses (0-96 h). This is the regimen the paper describes.
* **Daily dose at each water refresh (q12).** The same daily dose entered at
  every 12-h water refresh, ten doses (0-108 h). This doubles the total amount
  and is not a regimen the paper describes. It is included only because it is
  the reading under which the printed parameters reproduce the paper's own
  exposure (see Errata).

```{r regimens}
make_events <- function(daily_dose, reading, ids, obs_times) {
  if (reading == "Stated regimen (q24)") {
    dose_times <- seq(0, 96, by = 24)
  } else {
    dose_times <- seq(0, 108, by = 12)
  }
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = daily_dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}
readings <- c("Stated regimen (q24)", "Daily dose at each water refresh (q12)")
study_times <- c(
  0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 14, 24,
  120, 122, 124, 126, 132, 144, 152, 168, 174
)
```

# Typical-value exposure against the paper's NCA

For a linear model, the area under the whole concentration-time curve equals
the total absorbed dose divided by the apparent clearance,
`AUC0-inf = n_doses x D / (V/F x ke)`, whatever the dosing times. With the
printed `V/F` = 4.73 L/kg and `ke` = 0.154 1/h, `CL/F` = 0.728 L/kg/h. The
table compares that closed form, and the numerically integrated typical-value
profile, with the geometric-mean AUC0-inf of Supplementary Table S4.

```{r typical-auc}
mod <- readModelDb("Petkova_2022_doxycycline_chicken")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

cl_f <- 4.73 * 0.154
dense_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 200, by = 0.05), seq(200, 600, by = 1))))

typical_auc <- tidyr::expand_grid(groups, reading = readings) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_doses = ifelse(reading == readings[1], 5, 10),
    closed_form = n_doses * daily_dose / cl_f,
    numeric = {
      ev <- make_events(daily_dose, reading, 1L, dense_times)
      s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev))
      sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2)
    }
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Table S4, AUC0-inf geometric means (h*ug/mL)
table_s4 <- tibble::tibble(
  group = groups$group,
  cmax = c(3.11, 3.93, 2.32, 2.59),
  tmax = c(16.33, 13.82, 16.36, 16.11),
  aucinf.obs = c(293.21, 339.38, 288.19, 303.89)
)

typical_auc <- typical_auc |>
  dplyr::left_join(table_s4, by = "group") |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = closed_form / aucinf.obs)

typical_auc |>
  dplyr::select(group, reading, closed_form, numeric, aucinf.obs, ratio) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Group = group,
    `Dose records` = reading,
    `Model AUC0-inf, closed form` = closed_form,
    `Model AUC0-inf, integrated` = numeric,
    `Table S4 AUC0-inf` = aucinf.obs,
    `Model / Table S4` = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2),
    caption = "Typical-value AUC0-inf (h*ug/mL) under the two dose readings."
  )

stopifnot(
  # The integrated profile is the same parameters as the closed form; any gap
  # is pure numerical error (truncation at 600 h and the trapezoid).
  all(abs(typical_auc$numeric / typical_auc$closed_form - 1) < 0.01),
  # Stated regimen: the printed parameters give about half the observed AUC.
  all(typical_auc$ratio[typical_auc$reading == readings[1]] > 0.45),
  all(typical_auc$ratio[typical_auc$reading == readings[1]] < 0.60),
  # Daily dose at each refresh: within about 15% of every group.
  all(typical_auc$ratio[typical_auc$reading == readings[2]] > 0.90),
  all(typical_auc$ratio[typical_auc$reading == readings[2]] < 1.20)
)
```

Under the stated regimen the printed parameters give `r round(100 * min(typical_auc$ratio[typical_auc$reading == readings[1]]))`-`r round(100 * max(typical_auc$ratio[typical_auc$reading == readings[1]]))`%
of the observed AUC0-inf. Entering the daily dose at every water refresh gives
`r round(100 * min(typical_auc$ratio[typical_auc$reading == readings[2]]))`-`r round(100 * max(typical_auc$ratio[typical_auc$reading == readings[2]]))`%.

# Typical-value profiles against the observed data

```{r typical-profiles, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
typical_profiles <- tidyr::expand_grid(groups, reading = readings) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe({
    ev <- make_events(daily_dose, reading, 1L, seq(0, 180, by = 0.25))
    s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev))
    tibble::tibble(group = group, reading = reading, time = s$time, Cc = s$Cc)
  })

ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = dplyr::filter(observed, !blq),
    aes(time, conc),
    colour = "grey40",
    size = 1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = typical_profiles,
    aes(time, Cc, colour = reading),
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the start of treatment (h)",
    y = "Doxycycline plasma concentration (ug/mL)",
    colour = "Dose records"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The observed concentrations rise to about 2-3 ug/mL by 12-24 h and are still
about 2 ug/mL at the end of treatment (120 h). The typical profile under the
stated regimen peaks near 1 ug/mL after each dose; the daily-dose-every-12-h
reading roughly doubles it, to about the observed level.

# Visual predictive check

Figure 1b of the paper is a VPC of the pooled data (observed and predicted 10th,
50th and 90th percentiles). The simulation below gives 50 virtual birds per
group (200 per reading) the group's received dose under each reading, with the
full IIV and residual error, and compares the simulated percentiles with the
percentiles of the observed data at each sampling time.

```{r vpc, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20221111)
n_per_group <- 50

vpc_sim <- tidyr::expand_grid(groups, reading = readings) |>
  dplyr::mutate(row = dplyr::row_number()) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe({
    ids <- (row - 1) * n_per_group + seq_len(n_per_group)
    ev <- make_events(daily_dose, reading, ids, study_times[-1])
    s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev))
    tibble::tibble(
      group = group,
      reading = reading,
      id = as.integer(as.character(s$id)),
      time = s$time,
      Cc = s$Cc,
      sim = s$sim
    )
  })

pctl <- function(x, p) as.numeric(stats::quantile(x, p, na.rm = TRUE))
vpc_sim_summary <- vpc_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(reading, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p10 = pctl(sim, 0.1),
    p50 = pctl(sim, 0.5),
    p90 = pctl(sim, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
vpc_obs_summary <- observed |>
  dplyr::filter(!blq) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p10 = pctl(conc, 0.1),
    p50 = pctl(conc, 0.5),
    p90 = pctl(conc, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc_sim_summary, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = vpc_obs_summary, aes(y = p50), colour = "black") +
  geom_point(
    data = vpc_obs_summary,
    aes(y = p10),
    colour = "black",
    shape = 2,
    size = 1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = vpc_obs_summary,
    aes(y = p90),
    colour = "black",
    shape = 6,
    size = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~reading) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the start of treatment (h)",
    y = "Doxycycline plasma concentration (ug/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Shaded: simulated 10th-90th percentiles; line: simulated median.",
      "Points: observed 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles (Tables S2 and S3)."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Replicates Figure 1b of Petkova 2022. The paper's own VPC shows a predicted
median near 2 ug/mL through 24-120 h, in line with the observed data. Under
the stated regimen the packaged parameters give well under that level. The
daily-dose-every-12-h reading comes closer, particularly at the end of
treatment, but still sits below the observed medians on the first day, when
only one or two refresh doses have been given.

```{r vpc-check}
vpc_check <- vpc_sim_summary |>
  dplyr::inner_join(vpc_obs_summary, by = "time", suffix = c("_sim", "_obs")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    window = dplyr::case_when(
      time >= 12 & time <= 24 ~ "Day 1 (12-24 h)",
      time >= 120 & time <= 124 ~ "End of treatment (120-124 h)"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(window)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(reading, window) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_ratio = stats::median(p50_sim / p50_obs),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
vpc_check |>
  dplyr::rename(
    `Dose records` = reading,
    Window = window,
    `Simulated / observed median` = median_ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = "Ratio of simulated to observed median concentration, median over the sampling times in each window."
  )
ratio_q24 <- stats::median(vpc_check$median_ratio[vpc_check$reading == readings[1]])
ratio_q12 <- stats::median(vpc_check$median_ratio[vpc_check$reading == readings[2]])
stopifnot(
  # Stated regimen: well under half to two-thirds of the observed level.
  ratio_q24 < 0.65,
  # The doubled-dose reading roughly doubles the level (linear model).
  ratio_q12 / ratio_q24 > 1.5
)
```

# NCA against Supplementary Table S4

The paper's NCA (Phoenix, Section 2.5) used the study sampling times. The
individual predictions of the same 50 virtual birds per group are summarised
with PKNCA on the study grid (time zero added), with AUC0-inf computed over the whole profile and
extrapolated from the terminal phase after the last sample at 174 h.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- dplyr::select(vpc_sim, reading, group, id, time, Cc)

nca_conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_conc,
  dplyr::distinct(nca_conc, reading, group, id) |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste(reading, group, sep = " | ")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(treatment, id, time)

nca_dose <- dplyr::distinct(nca_conc, reading, group, treatment, id) |>
  dplyr::left_join(groups, by = "group") |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = daily_dose)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

reference <- tidyr::expand_grid(reading = readings, table_s4) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste(reading, group, sep = " | ")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs)

nca_table <- ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_res,
  reference,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "h*ug/mL")
)
nca_table |>
  dplyr::rename(`Dose records | group` = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = paste(
      "Simulated (median of 50 virtual birds per group) versus Table S4",
      "(geometric mean) NCA."
    )
  )
```

`r attr(nca_table, "footnote")`

```{r pknca-check}
nca_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = stats::median(PPORRES)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(reference, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    reading = sub(" \\| .*$", "", treatment),
    ratio = sim / aucinf.obs
  )
stopifnot(
  # A transcription or unit error would move these by tens of percent.
  stats::median(nca_auc$ratio[nca_auc$reading == readings[1]]) < 0.70,
  abs(stats::median(nca_auc$ratio[nca_auc$reading == readings[2]]) - 1) < 0.25
)
```

The observed Tmax of 14-16 h is an artefact of the sampling design: no sample
was taken between 24 and 120 h, so the observed peak is the highest of the
first-day samples. Under the stated regimen the simulated Tmax on the same grid
behaves the same way (12 h, just before the 24-h dose). Under the
daily-dose-every-12-h reading the last dose is at 108 h, so the 120-h sample is
the highest and the simulated Tmax is 120 h; the Tmax rows for that reading
reflect the dose timing, not the parameters. Under the stated regimen the
simulated Cmax and AUC0-inf are about 35-45% of the Table S4 values (the sparse
24-120 h gap also loses part of the inter-dose peaks that the closed-form AUC
above includes); under the daily-dose-every-12-h reading AUC0-inf agrees within
about 15% and Cmax within about 30%.

# Probability of target attainment (Table 3)

Section 2.7 simulated 5000 birds for 24 h at 1.5-h increments and computed the
percentage of the 24-h dosing interval with unbound concentration above the
MIC, with the unbound fraction fixed at 0.5. The chunk below repeats that on
200 virtual birds for the first 24 h after a 20 mg/kg dose, under both
readings, and also evaluates the paper's Equation 5,
`%T>MIC = ln(Dose x f / (V x MIC)) / ke x 100 / tau`, at the typical values.

```{r pta}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2440)
pta_times <- seq(0, 24, by = 1.5)
pta_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(readings, function(r) {
  dose_times <- if (r == readings[1]) 0 else c(0, 12)
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = 1:200, time = dose_times) |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = 20, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = 1:200, time = pta_times) |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev))
  tibble::tibble(reading = r, id = s$id, time = s$time, Cc = s$Cc)
}))

mics <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2)
quantile_probs <- c(0.95, 0.90, 0.75, 0.50, 0.25, 0.10, 0.05)
pta_ft <- function(r, m) {
  ft <- pta_sim |>
    dplyr::filter(reading == r, time < 24) |>
    dplyr::group_by(id) |>
    dplyr::summarise(ft = 100 * mean(0.5 * Cc > m))
  tibble::tibble(
    reading = r,
    mic = m,
    quantile = paste0(100 * (1 - quantile_probs), "%"),
    ft = as.numeric(stats::quantile(ft$ft, quantile_probs))
  )
}
pta_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(reading = readings, mic = mics)
pta_model <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  mapply(pta_ft, pta_grid$reading, pta_grid$mic, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
)

# Table 3 of Petkova 2022 (columns are the 5th..95th percentiles)
table3 <- tibble::tibble(
  mic = rep(mics, each = 7),
  quantile = rep(paste0(c(5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95), "%"), 4),
  ft = c(
    100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100,
    100, 100, 100, 100, 92.65, 79.60, 72.46,
    100, 91.89, 76.23, 62.07, 49.61, 40.23, 35.39,
    44.74, 38.05, 27.66, 17.50, 9.45, 4.35, 2.21
  )
)

pta_wide <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(table3, source = "Table 3"),
  dplyr::mutate(pta_model, source = reading) |> dplyr::select(-reading)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(quantile %in% c("10%", "50%", "90%")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = quantile, values_from = ft) |>
  dplyr::arrange(mic, source)
pta_wide |>
  dplyr::rename(`MIC (mg/L)` = mic, Source = source) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = c(2, 0, 1, 1, 1),
    caption = "%fT>MIC over the first 24 h: Table 3 versus the packaged model (10th, 50th and 90th percentile of birds)."
  )

eq5 <- tibble::tibble(
  `MIC (mg/L)` = mics,
  `Equation 5 at typical values (%)` = pmin(
    100,
    pmax(0, log(20 * 0.5 / (4.73 * mics)) / 0.154 * 100 / 24)
  )
)
knitr::kable(eq5, digits = c(2, 1), caption = "Paper Equation 5 at the typical V/F and ke.")
```

Table 3 cannot be reproduced from the printed parameters under either reading
or from Equation 5. Table 3 has 5% of birds above 2 ug/mL unbound (4 ug/mL
total) for 45% of the day, whereas the typical total concentration under the
stated regimen does not reach 1.5 ug/mL in the first 24 h. The table is shown
for completeness only.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dosing as oral boluses.** The drug was taken up with the drinking water
  across the day. The paper does not describe the dose records of its data set;
  the simulations enter each daily (or per-refresh) amount as an oral bolus
  into `depot`, which the absorption lag and slow `ka` (0.093 1/h) smooth into
  a near-continuous input.
* **Received doses.** The simulations use each group's actually received dose
  (Section 2.2: 24.41, 23.70, 22.18, 23.78 mg/kg/24 h), because "typical values
  of the pharmacokinetic parameters were calculated based on the actually
  received doses by every group" (Discussion).
* **Combined residual error.** Phoenix's additive + multiplicative error model
  is encoded as `combined2` (variance = `addSd^2 + (propSd x Cc)^2`).
* **Peripheral compartment specimen.** The unobserved peripheral compartment is
  labelled `tissue`.
* **Covariates.** Infection and NAC co-administration were screened and not
  retained; they are documented in `covariatesDataExcluded` as
  `DIS_INFECT_ACTIVE` and `CONMED_ACETYLCYSTEINE`. Body weight was not tested;
  all parameters are per kg.

# Errata

* **The printed parameters under-predict the paper's own exposure by about
  2-fold under the stated regimen.** `V/F x ke` = 0.728 L/kg/h, so five daily
  doses of 22-24 mg/kg give AUC0-inf of about 150-170 h*ug/mL, against
  288-339 h*ug/mL in Table S4 (ratio 0.48-0.57). The typical profile peaks near
  1.1 ug/mL against observed medians of about 2-3 ug/mL, and the paper's own
  Figure 1b VPC and Figure 2a PRED axis sit at the observed level. No reading of
  the stated regimen reconciles this: continuous zero-order intake over 120 h
  leaves the AUC unchanged (it is fixed by total dose / CL), dose in mg per bird
  with V in L per bird over-predicts by about 1.6-fold, and swapping `ka` and
  `ke` contradicts the Discussion ("a higher value of ka of 0.14 ... was
  obtained" in another study, implying ka < 0.14) and the abstract
  (`tvke` = 0.154 1/h). Entering the received daily dose at every 12-h water
  refresh reproduces the Table S4 AUC within about 15%. That
  suggests the published fit carried a doubled dose amount, in which case the
  shape parameters (`ka`, `k12`, `k21`, `tlag`, and `ke` as a rate) are usable
  but `V/F` and `CL/F` are about 2-fold too high for the true dose. The paper
  does not say how the dose records were built, so this remains a hypothesis.
  The model is packaged as printed and nothing has been tuned; do not use its
  absolute `V/F` or `CL/F` for dose prediction without this caveat.
* **Table 2 BSV (CV%) does not follow from the printed variances.** Equation 3,
  `CV% = 100 x sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`, turns the printed variances
  (0.002, 0.06, 1.02e-7, 0.32, 0.14, 0.79) into 4.5, 24.8, 0.03, 61.4, 38.8 and
  109.7%, not the printed 0.20, 6.40, 0.0001, 32.82, 14.27 and 93.17%. The
  packaged model uses the variance column, which is the quantity Phoenix
  estimates.
* **Table 1 confidence interval for `tvka`.** The printed 95% CI of 0.096-0.096
  does not contain the estimate 0.093 (SE 0.001); the estimate is used.
* **Table 3 is not reproducible** from the printed parameters under any reading
  tried, including the paper's Equation 5 (see the PTA section).
